text.p: Blue-chip stocks ended on a strong note Friday, regaining the previous session's steep losses as the August jobs numbers eased Wall Street's worst fears about a sharp rise in interest rates by the Federal Reserve.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 52.90 points at 5,659.86, bouncing back from Thursday's 50-point fall. For the week, the Dow was up 43.65 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 1,645 to 693 on moderate volume of 348 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said stocks shadowed the rebound in bonds after a key report on hourly wages soothed the frayed nerves of inflation-wary investors.
The market is now betting on a modest rise of one-quarter percentage point in interest rates compared with recent talk that it could be a sharp increase of one-half percentage point.

"We dodged a major bullet," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "At worst we'll see a 25 basis point (one-quarter percentage point) increase at the Sept. 24 meeting."
"I think the equity markets followed the sigh of relief breathed by the bond market today," he said.
The Labour Department report said the jobless rate fell to 5.1 percent in August, and non-farm payrolls rose by 250,000, about even with economists' estimates.
The drop in the unemployment rate, brought the jobless rate to its lowest level since March 1989, when it was 5 percent, the department said.
Average hourly earnings of workers rose to $11.87 in August from $11.81 in July.

The upward pressure on wages, including a 50-cent-an-hour increase in the government-mandated minimum wage on Oct. 1, comes at a time when prices for food and energy are also showing signs of rising, which could prod the Fed to raise interest rates to stem inflationary pressures.
A decision on raising interest rates could come out of the the Fed's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Sept. 24.
Analysts said because stocks and bonds had sold off steeply Thursday out of fear an extremely strong report, traders took solace in the report's merely mildly surprising strength.
"Yesterday, everybody sold off ahead of the numbers and now the numbers came in fairly decent," said Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities.
Markets had focused almost obsessively on the employment report for several reasons.
Economists believed that indications of coming inflation would first be felt in upward pressures on wages with labour markets becoming ever tighter.

Ironically, the strength of the jobs report also convinced many that a Fed tightening was more likely than ever, but because markets had apparently priced in a steep increase, analysts seized on the bright side of the data.

In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond rose more than half a point, and its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, fell to 7.11 percent from 7.15 percent at Thursday's close.
Financial and transportation stocks, both of which are sensitive to interest rates, rebounded.
J.P. Morgan & Co. gained 1-3/8 to 88-3/8 and Chase Manhattan Corp. jumped 1-3/8 to 75-1/4. Delta Air Lines Inc. climbed 1-1/4 to 68-1/8 and United Airlines' parent UAL Corp. rose 1-3/4 to 46-7/8.

In other individual issues, International Business Machines Corp. rose 2-1/8 to 115-1/4. Traders cited positive comments by Prudential Securities analyst Don Young about IBM's mainframe upgrade announcement, which is due next week.
Young was not available to comment but his office confirmed that he commented favourably about the new mainframe models, which have been widely anticipated by Wall Street.
Gap Inc. gained 1-1/2 to 30-1/2, in a partial rebound from Thursday when investors dumped the shares after the company reported flat August same-store sales.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 13.73 to 1,139.39.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 6.24 points to 655.68. The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.31 to 560.02.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.03 to 352.67. The average share was up 33 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,449.752 up 55.092 or 0.86 percent.
